name: Acquired Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder with Decreased Elastic Tissue

criteria.description: Presence of asymptomatic, finely wrinkled, lax skin predominantly on the neck, upper trunk, or flexural areas
Skin biopsy demonstrating decreased or fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis without significant inflammation
Exclusion of inherited elastin disorders and other causes of elastolysis such as cutis laxa or pseudoxanthoma elasticum
No evidence of systemic connective tissue disease or internal organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation combined with histopathological confirmation and exclusion of other elastolytic disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized dermal elastolysis with decreased elastic fibers
Fine wrinkling and laxity of affected skin areas
searchTerms: skin with fine wrinkles and looseness

common.symptomName: Asymptomatic skin changes without pruritus or pain
searchTerms: skin changes without itching or pain

common.symptomName: Predominant involvement of neck and upper trunk skin
searchTerms: skin changes mainly on neck and upper back
neck and upper trunk skin involvement
localized skin issues on upper body

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin atrophy in affected areas
History of sun exposure in affected regions
searchTerms: history of sun damage in spots
skin changes linked to sun exposure

rare.symptomName: Secondary mild inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
searchTerms: mild inflammation seen on skin biopsy
slight immune cell presence in skin

rare.symptomName: Associated mild telangiectasia in affected skin
searchTerms: small visible blood vessels in skin

imaging: Not typically required; skin biopsy is diagnostic
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; acquired disorder
other: Histopathology showing decreased or fragmented elastic fibers in dermis using special stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson)

distinguishingFeatures: Inherited or acquired generalized skin laxity
Systemic involvement including pulmonary and cardiovascular complications
Histology shows fragmented elastic fibers with systemic manifestations
Calcification and fragmentation of elastic fibers
Characteristic yellow papules and plaques in flexural areas
Selective loss of elastic fibers in mid-dermis
Fine wrinkling predominantly on trunk and upper extremities
Histopathology differentiates from other elastolytic disorders

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as dyspnea or cardiovascular abnormalities
Presence of skin calcifications or papular lesions
references: Uitto J, et al. Elastic fiber biology and cutaneous disorders. J Invest Dermatol. 2017.
